hero.title: Resource Library
hero.subtitle: Keeps database listings, the skills list, variable discovery, project records, and conversation lessons in one archive. Variable work starts from PubMed monitoring, moves through candidate extraction, human review, and evidence alignment, then lands in the variable overview; project reports, dataset indexes, and correction lessons are preserved for direct reuse.
workflow: Use databases and skills as a reusable resource base
Discover candidate variables from PubMed updates, review them, then merge into the variable overview
Preserve project reports, stage summaries, and dataset indexes
Turn correction lessons and conversation memory into reusable rules

variableKnowledge.lead: Variables and PubMed discovery now live inside the Resource Library: start blank, run PubMed discovery, manually review candidates, then promote accepted variables into the overview.
variableKnowledge.overviewLead: Reviewed variable tags live here so naming stays consistent across projects. Candidates that pass discovery review are promoted into this list.
variableKnowledge.discoveryLead: Candidate variables are extracted from PubMed literature, enter a human review queue, and only then are promoted into variable tags.

footnote.databases: Use this database list as a quick map of official entry points and dataset scope. Always follow each source's data-use agreement and citation rules.
footnote.skills: Use the skills list to browse and reuse Agent capability guides. Verify trusted sources before importing or editing local skills, and follow applicable licenses when citing external skills.
footnote.variableOverview: The variable overview lists reviewed variable tags for consistent naming and reuse. Always verify against original literature and database field definitions before extraction or analysis.
footnote.variableDiscovery: Variable discovery extracts candidate variables from PubMed literature and requires manual review before promotion. Do not use unreviewed candidates for formal analysis or publication.
footnote.reports: Memory summary archives project materials and conversation lessons for reuse. Verify original files and evidence sources before formal citation or publication.

mirroredDatabases.title: Databases
mirroredDatabases.lead: Grouped by research scenario, the catalog currently includes {{count}} database sources spanning critical-care EHR, aging panels, cancer surveillance, population health, and socioeconomic surveys.
mirroredDatabases.routeHint: Use this as the local extraction source name. Before extraction, verify access approval, version, and schema.
mirroredDatabases.checklistBody: Confirm access authorization, version/wave, sample grain, timeline semantics, join keys, missing-value rules, and citation requirements before variable search or small-scale extraction.

sections.title: Critical care & ICU EHR databases
sections.lead: MIMIC releases, NWICU, eICU, and PIC ICU/EHR sources. Confirm patient, admission, ICU/PICU stay, event tables, and timeline semantics before extraction; do not mix schema assumptions across versions.

items.name: MIMIC-III
items.summary: Classic ICU EHR database for reproducing earlier critical-care studies, diagnosis/treatment/lab trajectories, and ICU outcome models. Use the independent mimiciii source and version-specific schema.
items.usagePolicy: Requires the user to complete PhysioNet credentialing, CITI/equivalent training, and the applicable DUA. Use only a lawfully obtained copy within the approved research scope; do not share accounts, credentials, or raw data.

items.name: MIMIC-IV 1.0
items.summary: PhysioNet MIMIC-IV 1.0 database organized around core, hosp, and icu modules with patient, admission, stay, and event-level tables for ICU trajectories, labs, and treatments.
items.usagePolicy: Requires independent PhysioNet credentialing, CITI/equivalent training, and the applicable DUA. Version, module, and citation rules must follow the official page; the platform does not fetch or redistribute raw data.

items.name: MIMIC-IV 3.1
items.summary: Newer local MIMIC-IV entry. Re-check variables through the 3.1 schema, concept, join, and guardrail indexes instead of reusing MIMIC-IV 1.0 table assumptions.
items.usagePolicy: Use only after independent authorization for the official MIMIC-IV 3.1 release and re-check the 3.1 schema. Do not mix 1.0 authorization, table assumptions, or data copies with this version.

items.name: NWICU
items.summary: Northwestern Memorial HealthCare de-identified ICU/EHR data from 2020-2022. The local entry includes hosp and icu modules with admissions, patients, labevents, diagnoses, prescriptions, eMAR, ICU stays, charted events, and procedure events; use the independent nwicu source to verify table grain, join keys, and time fields.
items.usagePolicy: A restricted PhysioNet health dataset. Users must independently complete access requirements and upload their lawful copy; outputs must not expose re-identifying information or raw tables.

items.name: eICU-CRD
items.summary: Multi-center ICU database where many analyses depend on `patientunitstayid` and ICU-relative offset semantics for charted and treatment events.
items.usagePolicy: Requires PhysioNet credentialed access and the applicable DUA. Do not redistribute patientunitstayid-level raw data or credentials, and follow official citation requirements in publications.

items.name: PIC
items.summary: Paediatric Intensive Care database from the Children's Hospital, Zhejiang University School of Medicine, with demographics, admissions, PICU stays, labs, medication, symptoms, surgery, and event tables. Confirm patient/admission/PICU-stay grain and pediatric timeline semantics before extraction.
items.usagePolicy: Follow PhysioNet/PICDB restricted-data terms. Pediatric ICU data must remain within de-identified research boundaries, with no re-identification attempts or raw-data sharing.

sections.title: Cancer registries & global cancer statistics
sections.lead: GCO / GLOBOCAN provides country- and region-level incidence, mortality, prevalence, and projection statistics, while SEER provides tumor-level U.S. registry research data. Distinguish aggregate statistics from tumor records and verify release, year coverage, staging conventions, and access agreements.

items.name: GCO / GLOBOCAN
items.summary: IARC global cancer statistics source. The current query pack covers GLOBOCAN 2022 v1.1, CI5plus October 2024, and UNDP HDR 2021–22 for incidence, mortality, prevalence, cancer rankings, and 2022–2050 projections.
items.usagePolicy: Follow IARC/GCO terms for use, citation, and redistribution, and identify the exact data product and version in outputs. The local gco source allows filtered queries only; full extraction and bulk download are disabled.

items.name: SEER Research Data (17 Registries)
items.summary: U.S. NCI tumor-registry research data. The current local query pack uses the November 2025 submission for 17 registries and tumor records diagnosed in 2000–2023, including demographics, cancer site, stage, treatment, and survival fields.
items.usagePolicy: Every data user must apply separately and accept the current SEER Data Use Agreement. Research Plus, NCCR, and specialized databases have additional account and location restrictions. Do not share accounts or raw data, attempt re-identification, or perform prohibited person-level linkage.

sections.title: International aging longitudinal panels
sections.lead: SHARE, HRS, ELSA, KLoSA, LASI, MHAS, and related international aging panels. Route by country, wave, sample grain, and weighting; check comparability before cross-cohort analyses.

items.name: ELSA
items.summary: English Longitudinal Study of Ageing, with repeated measures of health, social participation, and retirement transitions for trajectory-focused aging analyses.
items.usagePolicy: Usually obtained through UK Data Service or another official channel under licence. Follow the End User Licence, do not redistribute, and cite ELSA/UKDS as required.

items.name: HRS
items.summary: Health and Retirement Study in the U.S., a foundational panel for aging, cognition, family, and wealth dynamics across waves.
items.usagePolicy: Requires registration through the HRS official data portal and acceptance of data-use terms. Use only for permitted research/teaching purposes; do not redistribute or re-identify.

items.name: KLoSA
items.summary: Korean Longitudinal Study of Aging for East-Asian aging trajectories, labor exit, and social support analyses with wave-aware extraction.
items.usagePolicy: Obtain data through KEIS/KLoSA official channels and follow their download and use rules. Cross-wave analyses should report wave, sample, and weighting choices.

items.name: LASI
items.summary: Longitudinal Aging Study in India, covering chronic disease, functional status, and household support for LMIC aging comparisons.
items.usagePolicy: Obtain through IIPS/LASI or an authorized data platform under its access rules. Do not resell, redistribute, or identify respondents; acknowledge and cite the official project.

items.name: MHAS
items.summary: Mexican Health and Aging Study, suited for chronic burden, functional outcomes, and family-care structure analyses in Latin America.
items.usagePolicy: Use data downloaded/registered through official MHAS channels under their conditions. Do not redistribute, and cite the relevant wave, data files, and project source.

items.name: SHARE
items.summary: Survey of Health, Ageing and Retirement in Europe, enabling country-comparative policy and health-inequality analyses across harmonized waves.
items.usagePolicy: Requires SHARE Research Data Center registration and acceptance of the Conditions of Use. Use is for scientific research only; redistribution, commercial resale, and re-identification are prohibited.

sections.title: China aging longitudinal panels
sections.lead: CHARLS, CLHLS, and CLASS support China aging-health research on retirement, family support, mortality, disability, ADL, cognition, social participation, and healthy-aging trajectories.

items.name: CHARLS
items.summary: China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study: adults 45+ and spouses, covering health, economics, family, retirement, and social participation for aging research in China.
items.usagePolicy: Users or institutions must register, apply, and accept terms through the CHARLS official site. Do not share data-access credentials or provide copies to unauthorized people.

items.name: CLHLS
items.summary: Chinese Longitudinal Healthy Longevity Survey for oldest-old and longevity research, including mortality, disability, ADL, cognition, and determinants of healthy aging.
items.usagePolicy: Apply and cite through the CLHLS official data platform/project rules. Maintain anonymity for older-adult respondent data and do not transmit individual-level raw data.

items.name: CLASS
items.summary: Chinese Longitudinal Aging Social Survey, a continuing nationwide survey led by Renmin University of China. The current query pack covers five waves—2014, 2016, 2018, 2020, and 2023—for health, aging support, economics, family, and social participation research.
items.usagePolicy: Obtain and use the data under the official CLASS application instructions, checking approved waves and versions. Do not provide person-level raw data or credentials to unauthorized people or attempt respondent identification.

sections.title: UKB / NHANES
sections.lead: UK Biobank multimodal cohort and U.S. NHANES representative health surveys. Confirm field/instance/array coverage, cycle, weights, and endpoint sources in the local package.

items.name: UK Biobank
items.summary: Large UK prospective cohort with genetics, imaging, and linked health records; the local package may also include matched proteomics / Olink layers.
items.usagePolicy: Requires an approved project through the UK Biobank Access Management System and the applicable access/material agreement. Use is limited to approved purposes, approved researchers, and authorized fields.

items.name: NHANES
items.summary: U.S. National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey: nationally representative cross-sectional waves with exams, labs, and questionnaires for U.S. population health research.
items.usagePolicy: Public-use files still require CDC/NCHS citation, confidentiality, and survey-design compliance. Do not attempt respondent re-identification; report cycle, weights, and sampling design.

sections.title: China community health & nutrition surveys
sections.lead: CHNS and related community/household health, diet, exam, and policy-change data. Analyses often require explicit joins across topic sub-tables; confirm wave and table structure first.

items.name: CHNS
items.summary: China Health and Nutrition Survey: longitudinal community and household data on health, diet, physical exam, and policy change, typically requiring explicit joins across topic sub-tables.
items.usagePolicy: Obtain through the UNC/CPC CHNS official channel and follow data-use and citation requirements. Do not redistribute household/person-level data; report survey year and table source.

sections.title: China household panel & general social surveys
sections.lead: CFPS and CGSS cover household, person-level, social attitude, stratification, and quality-of-life topics. Distinguish panel data from repeated cross-sections before variable search.

items.name: CFPS
items.summary: China Family Panel Studies: longitudinal microdata on families and individuals for economics, education, health, and social change.
items.usagePolicy: Register/apply through the official CFPS data platform and follow the user agreement. Do not transfer, share, or commercialize raw microdata.

items.name: CGSS
items.summary: Chinese General Social Survey: repeated cross-sections on social attitudes, stratification, and quality of life.
items.usagePolicy: Obtain through the official CGSS data platform under its user agreement. Cite survey year/version and the official source; do not transmit raw data.

sections.title: China finance, income & labor surveys
sections.lead: CHFS, CHIP, CLDS, and CSS cover household finance, income distribution, labor-force dynamics, and national social conditions. Confirm person/household/community grain, year scope, and weights before extraction.

items.name: CHFS
items.summary: China Household Finance Survey: assets, debt, income, consumption, and financial behavior at household level.
items.usagePolicy: Use under the official CHFS data-application and user-agreement rules. Household finance microdata must not be sold, rented, transferred, or provided to unauthorized third parties.

items.name: CHIP
items.summary: Chinese Household Income Project: income distribution, inequality, and household surveys coordinated with institutional partners in China.
items.usagePolicy: Obtain through official CHIP/China income-distribution research channels and follow data-use restrictions. Do not redistribute; protect respondent anonymity in income microdata analyses.

items.name: CLDS
items.summary: China Labor-force Dynamics Survey: employment, mobility, and labor market outcomes (Sun Yat-sen University).
items.usagePolicy: Apply through official channels such as the Sun Yat-sen University survey center and follow the user agreement. Do not share raw individual, household, or community-level data.

items.name: CSS
items.summary: Chinese Social Survey: national social conditions and public opinion (Renmin University of China).
items.usagePolicy: Obtain through the official survey/data platform and follow data-use rules. Use only within the authorized research scope and cite as required by the project.

indicators.title: Common clinical & population-health metrics
indicators.lead: Typical operationalizations in cohort and claims studies—align with your protocol’s time zero, units, and missing-data rules.

items.name: eGFR (CKD-EPI / MDRD)
items.summary: Estimated GFR from creatinine (equation version sets covariates); CKD staging and drug safety analyses.

items.name: BMI
items.summary: Weight (kg) / height (m)²; survey and cohort stratification; not a direct adiposity measure.

items.name: Blood pressure / hypertension control
items.summary: JNC/ACC-AHA thresholds vary by guideline; NHANES and many cohorts support standardized seated BP protocols.

items.name: Charlson / Elixhauser
items.summary: Comorbidity scores from diagnosis codes for risk adjustment in administrative and EHR-linked research.

items.name: ASCVD / Framingham-style risk
items.summary: 10-year cardiovascular risk tools using traditional factors; choose the equation that matches your population and guideline context.

items.name: ADL / IADL disability scales
items.summary: Activity limitations in aging surveys (e.g. CHARLS, CLHLS, HRS family); core for dependency and care demand analyses.

diseases.title: High-volume themes in public-health data
diseases.lead: Frequent topics in national surveys and aging cohorts—useful for keyword scoping and comparator selection.

items.name: Cardiometabolic disease
items.summary: Hypertension, diabetes, dyslipidemia, obesity; tightly linked to NHANES labs and self-report in many national surveys.

items.name: Aging & disability
items.summary: Cognitive decline, falls, care needs; central to CHARLS, CLHLS, and comparable longitudinal studies.

items.name: Healthcare access & insurance
items.summary: Coverage, OOP costs, and utilization—common in household finance and retirement surveys.

items.name: Mental health & well-being
items.summary: Depression and anxiety symptom scales appear across CGSS, CFPS health modules, and aging cohorts.
